breaks.quote: If the answer is no, prune. Pick something that still matters to you and prune it.
breaks.why: The ask rests on the writer's one story plus a short paragraph about the reader's list, so a doubtful reader can shrug and keep everything.

breaks.quote: Don't wait for it to become useless first, because you may never be able to call any of them useless.
breaks.why: The reader's strongest doubt (ending things that still matter) gets one sentence of reasoning, which names the answer without arguing it.

breaks.quote: Pruning hurts, and it will hurt you too. But what you truly need, you can go back to
breaks.why: The cost is stated as pain and then waved off with a promise of restarting, and the ask is squeezed into the last lines without a built case for why this change and not an easier one.
